selection_rule: PRE-COMMITTED before any sampled row was read: from bench/memory/results/2026-09-09-p1-195034/judged.jsonl in file order, take rows at 0-based index i where i % 5 == 3 (i.e. rows 3, 8, 13, ..., 98) — the SAME deterministic rule lane 167 used on run 2026-09-08-p1-185920 (every 5th judged row, phase 3). The file holds 100 rows with arm 'mem0' occupying indices 0-49 and arm 'mem0-raw' indices 50-99, so the sample is 10 rows per arm, drawn evenly through each arm's block. Disclosure: the task brief asked for '20 items per run, 5 per arm'; on a two-arm file those two clauses cannot both hold, and the brief's binding constraints (same rule as 167, quoted; 20 items per run) fix this sampling — 10 per arm, not 5. File index is the only selection key — question text, gold, answer, question_type and judge labels play no part in which rows are sampled.
scoring_protocol: Each item was hand-scored EXACT / PARTIAL / WRONG from the question, the gold reference answer and the model answer ONLY, applying the same rubric the local judge was given (bench/memory/judge.mjs judgePrompt, judge-prompt.2): WRONG leads — an answer that does not state the gold fact is WRONG, never PARTIAL (refusals, 'not in my memory', restated context without the fact, a different question, a different fact); PARTIAL requires part of the gold fact correctly on the table (name without date, number off only by rounding, one of two items); EXACT states the gold fact, essentially equivalent wording fine. The judge's emitted label (and judge_raw) for the sampled rows was NOT read before scoring; labels below were written into this file before the rejudge command was run, and were never revised afterwards.
